```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(tidyverse); library(cluster); library(factoextra); library(corrplot)
source("R/helpers.R")
```

# 1. Introduction
Customer segmentation divides customers into groups with similar behaviour so that a business can target each group with suitable marketing. This project applies **K-Means clustering** in **R** to mall customer data.

# 2. Objectives
- Explore the customer data.
- Find the best number of clusters.
- Build and profile customer segments.
- Suggest marketing strategies and build an interactive Shiny dashboard.

# 3. Dataset
```{r data}
df <- load_data()
glimpse(df)
summary(df)
colSums(is.na(df))
```

# 4. Exploratory Data Analysis
```{r eda}
ggplot(df, aes(Age, fill = Gender)) + geom_histogram(bins = 15, colour = "white", position = "dodge") + theme_minimal()
ggplot(df, aes(Income, Spending, colour = Gender)) + geom_point(size = 2) + theme_minimal()
corrplot(cor(df[, c("Age", "Income", "Spending")]), method = "color", addCoef.col = "black")
```

# 5. Choosing K
```{r k}
scaled <- scale(df[, c("Age", "Income", "Spending")])
set.seed(123)
fviz_nbclust(scaled, kmeans, method = "wss", k.max = 10)
fviz_nbclust(scaled, kmeans, method = "silhouette", k.max = 10)
```

# 6. K-Means Clustering
```{r km}
res <- run_kmeans(df, k = 5)
fviz_cluster(res$model, data = scaled, geom = "point", ellipse.type = "convex", ggtheme = theme_minimal())
```

# 7. Segment Profile
```{r profile}
knitr::kable(res$profile)
ggplot(res$data, aes(Income, Spending, colour = Segment)) + geom_point(size = 2) + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# 8. Business Recommendations
| Segment | Strategy |
|---|---|
| Premium Spenders | Loyalty programme, early access, premium offers |
| Careful Wealthy | Quality-focused personalised campaigns |
| Budget Enthusiasts | Discounts, coupons, EMI and festival sales |
| Low-Value Savers | Low-cost promotions only |
| Standard Customers | Seasonal offers, cross-selling |

# 9. Conclusion
K-Means divided the customers into distinct, interpretable segments. The results help the business plan targeted marketing. **Future scope:** hierarchical clustering comparison, PCA, deployment of the Shiny app online.

# 10. References
- Kaggle: Mall Customer Segmentation Data
- R Documentation: `stats::kmeans`, `factoextra`, `shiny`
